obligation: CBP breach notice by a customs broker
trigger: Any known breach of electronic or physical records relating to the broker's customs business (CBP intends the common meaning of breach; no materiality test). Clock starts at discovery
notify: CBP Security Operations Center, by email to cbpsoc@cbp.dhs.gov, with any known compromised importer identification numbers (19 CFR 24.5: EINs, or SSNs for six individual importers). Questions by phone to the number posted on CBP.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - licensed broker. The archive and laptop hold records for about 40 clients

deadline: Updated list of additional compromised importer identification numbers within 10 business days of the notification; any other new information within 72 hours of its discovery

trigger: Unauthorized access to electronic personal information of Florida residents (for this business: name with Social Security number for the individual importers; name with financial account number and access code would also count)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. No notice needed if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the business determines in writing that identity theft or financial harm is not likely; keep that determination 5 years and send it to the Department within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the individual importers' records were accessed. The deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) is not relied on: CBP's rule requires notice to CBP, not to individuals (counsel confirms)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - personal information of about 6 individuals is held; recheck the count

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the business has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after the vendor determines the breach or has reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - customs software vendor, email and file suite provider, accounting SaaS provider

trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (one individual importer lives in another state)
notify: Residents and regulators under the law of each state where affected individuals reside
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of each affected individual

citation: Client terms; CTPAT importer business partner security agreements (N48-49-R05)
deadline: As each agreement states; one CTPAT importer's agreement asks for notice within 24 hours of a known incident affecting its data

obligation: Report of a cyber incident involving or endangering a port, vessel, or waterfront facility
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering any vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility, including systems there
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Captain of the Port
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the evidence shows the incident reaches or threatens port or terminal systems (for example, stolen credentials for a terminal or port community portal). Counsel decides; when in doubt, report

obligation: USCG reportable cyber incident to the National Response Center
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a vessel or facility covered by Subpart F that was not reported under 33 CFR 6.16-1
deadline: Not applicable here (owner or operator duty under Subpart F)
applies_at_this_tier: No - Subpart F does not apply (no vessel or facility security plan; P03 G-001)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability

trigger: Ransomware, extortion, or a fraudulent wire
deadline: As soon as possible; for a fraudulent wire, call the bank first so it can try to recall the funds
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and fund recovery
Only if coverage exists - no cyber policy; check the broker's professional liability policy for a cyber or funds transfer fraud endorsement

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated rail, transit, or pipeline operator
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification (SD Sec. II.C; verified for SD 1580-21-01E and SD Pipeline-2021-01G 2026-10-05); supplemental information within 24 hours of it becoming available

citation: TSA airport and aircraft operator security programs (SSI)
trigger: Significant cybersecurity incident at a regulated airport or aircraft operator
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an airport or aircraft operator

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or services found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts
